### ۱۸. جزئیات اجرایی باز و موضوعات نیازمند اعتبارسنجی
### ۱۹. مسیر مفهومی توسعه و نسبت آن با مرحله‌بندی مصوب
### ۲۰. الزامات الحاق و سازگاری با سند قبلی
## فصل سوم — معماری تفصیلی ایجنت‌های دامنه‌محور و اجرای خدمات

tables.description: Data domain, logical owner and primary proposed location

executable_decisions.decision: Separate Core/Adviser data ownership and tables; prohibit direct cross-service table access; local transactions; Outbox for reliable events; idempotent consumers; durable service-owned jobs; authenticated versioned sync APIs; async jobs for long work; resilience and privacy-safe telemetry.
R1 deploys only Core and Adviser; shared host/PostgreSQL/Redis permitted with logical isolation; logical data responsibility does not itself grant deployment boundary or direct access.

Use PostgreSQL as operational and PostgreSQL-first knowledge baseline; Neo4j is not approved or an R1 prerequisite; document repository stores full text and versions; exchange via authorized versioned APIs; prohibit direct cross-service table access and public-index merging of personal data.

Contracts define owner/consumer, contract ID/version, purpose/minimal fields, authorization/identity, data version/freshness, errors/recovery; incompatible changes require version/migration; sensitive missing data/access leads to explicit error, completion or safe stop; broker/distributed transactions are not mandatory.

A05 local transaction boundary; Transactional Outbox for reliable publication; controlled eventual consistency for non-sensitive data; stable published snapshot and rules version for loan calculations; Adviser uses synchronous Core API; monitoring excludes sensitive payload; technology thresholds remain open.
Repeat authorization check before every sensitive action; evidence-based feedback is allowed in Bronze/Silver/Gold; feedforward only Silver/Gold under E01 and D01-D03.
Alternative loan may be proposed, but addition requires customer approval and does not stop remaining loan flows; distinguish missing document, unmet condition and unavailable bank service.
R1 has domain-icon home and domain chat; Adviser entry is not mandatory; only Adviser is active in R1; Assistant tab may say coming soon.

Domain suggestion requires user confirmation; domain remains fixed in session; role changes require explicit user action; out-of-domain independent requests do not receive specialist answer; transfer requires user action; same-domain context may be minimally retrieved after access check; cross-domain transfer requires scoped consent; role change does not transfer execution authority; Assistant not deployed in R1.
Acceptance thresholds, sampling method and target values are set after real experiments.
Open question: final plan/service/prompt prices.
Open question: exact services and plan scope.
Plan access remains an open design detail, but independent out-of-domain requests are prohibited; cross-domain subtask requires specialized contract and separate authorization.

Retention numbers, priority thresholds, retry timing, SMS cost/conditions are open; D03 lifecycle/dedup/quality/channel/history principles, D02 alert conditions, and D01 capability separation are approved; plan quotas remain open.
Open question: authorization and customer representation levels.
Open question: permitted Computer Use access and availability of bank product APIs.
A04 PostgreSQL job-state authority and Port/Adapter isolation are fixed; queue/worker technology and Temporal migration criteria remain open.
Open question: Neo4j data model, deployment and operating cost.
B05 architecture and automation policy approved; retention/deletion, memory/transfer contracts, sensitive-data processing basis, controls and legal retention details remain open.

A01 target architecture is fixed; module boundaries, contracts, control implementation, resource/operational cost, resilience, existing-infrastructure tests and separation/migration criteria remain open.

The conceptual dependency list is not the approved three-stage release plan; commercial/financial capabilities activate only in a release needing them after independent gates; no automatic stage four.

The historical conceptual order is not binding release order or approved task; first RAG release deploys Core and Adviser only; wallet/payments/commercial plans and Assistant are not prerequisites; domain-based home and Adviser with embedded recommender are R1 scope.
Preserve chapter one Demand-Driven Hybrid RAG, discovery, revalidation and relationship discovery.
Plans, wallet, pricing and permissions are product architecture, not UI-only settings.
Backend locks the domain selected/confirmed; no independent out-of-domain request, even in Gold; cross-domain contractual prerequisite does not change session domain or authorize destination tools.
Computer Use is the operational execution backbone; bank API is a complementary option for catalog data updates/commercial opportunity.
Frontend changes are not prerequisite to core phase-two execution.
Conflicts must be reported; no existing principle changes without review and approval.
Record every decision with status agreed, proposed, needs validation or open.
Do not centralize law interpretation, authorization, debiting and bank operations in one agent; AI coordinates/analyzes while sensitive controls remain deterministic, testable and auditable.

Chapter 3 design must align with Core/Adviser/Assistant boundaries; Adviser independent from Core in R1; Assistant not deployed until its release; diagrams of extractable monolith are logical/history, not alternate deployment decision.

Agents/tools consume only evidence permitted by publication, authorization, scope, time and Claim-Level Citation Guard; web/document content is not executable instruction; financial calculations use deterministic versioned tools; user authorization and safe stop are independent of RAG evidence.
Architecture/product rules with approval IDs are in force; execution tools, OS capabilities and bank interactions require validation; chapter is neither implementation instruction nor legal approval.
